--- title: "[StepMutate]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Apply arbitrary column expressions — the escape hatch. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/step_mutate.py#L71-L238){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python StepMutate(mutations, *, role="predictor", id=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Each supplied mutation either adds a new column or overwrites an existing one, so the exact column change is only known after the mutations run on the training frame. `fit()` applies them once to read off which columns were *added* (and their dtypes) versus modified in place, then re-applies the same expressions at transform time. New columns are attributed to no declared parents (``output_parents`` maps each to ``[]``): the expressions are opaque callables, so shoez does not try to infer which inputs a mutation read. This is the deliberate trade-off of an escape hatch — full flexibility, coarse lineage. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [mutations]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Mapping[str, Mutation]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mapping from output column name to a callable taking the frame and returning that column's value (a narwhals expression or series). Must be a non-empty ``dict`` of ``str`` names to callables. [role]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["predictor"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Role assigned to any *new* columns the mutations create. Columns overwritten in place keep their existing role. Default ``"predictor"``. [id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Stable step identifier. Default ``"mutate"``. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ``x_sq`` is added from an expression over ``x``; ``x`` itself is overwritten in place: ::: {#dc8edd7c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]}) df ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
x
0 1.0
1 2.0
2 3.0
``` ::: ::: Specifying the step touches no data: ::: {#387c4761 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} recipe = Recipe().add( StepMutate({"x_sq": lambda df: df["x"] ** 2, "x": lambda df: df["x"] + 1}) ) recipe ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` Recipe (untrained) Inputs: no roles assigned Steps: step_mutate() [untrained] ``` ::: ::: `fit()` runs the mutations once on the training frame to read off which columns they add and with what dtypes: ::: {#17084041 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted = recipe.fit(df) fitted ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` Recipe (trained) Inputs: 2 columns — 2 predictors Steps: step_mutate(x → x_sq) [trained] ``` ::: ::: `transform()` applies them together, so every mutation sees the original frame; ``x_sq`` squares the incoming ``x``, not the overwritten one: ::: {#fe4d098f .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fitted.transform(df) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
x x_sq
0 2.0 1.0
1 3.0 4.0
2 4.0 9.0
``` ::: :::
